extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (U.S. patent attorneys/agents, inventors)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and formal standards for filing U.S. patent applications (oaths/declarations, specification, claims, title/abstract, application data sheet, and related formalities) as set out in MPEP §§1.63–1.76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution/signature of oath or declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must be executed (i.e., signed) in accordance with § 1.66 or § 1.68; execution may alternatively be by an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no minimum age for a person to sign, but the signer must be competent to understand the document. Oaths/affirmations made before authorized officers (see §1.66) must be attested by proper official seal or other competent evidence of official character if no seal is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor identification in oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration must identify each inventor by full name, including the family name and at least one given name without abbreviation together with any other given name or initial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification requirement ensures correct named inventorship for the application record (§1.63(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor citizenship identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration must identify the country of citizenship of each inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required bibliographic element in the oath/declaration (§1.63(a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration must identify the application and affirm review
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration must identify the application to which it is directed and state that the person making it has reviewed and understands the contents of the application, including the claims, as amended by any amendment specifically referred to in the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement appears in §1.63(b)(1)-(2) and ensures the signer is aware of the application content being attested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of duty to disclose (duty of candor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration must state that the person making it acknowledges the duty to disclose to the Office all information known to the person to be material to patentability as defined in §1.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of §1.63(b)(3). Compliance relates to the duty of candor/inequitable conduct standards and must be expressly acknowledged in the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact/mailing/residence information in oath (unless ADS used)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless supplied on an application data sheet (§1.76), the oath/declaration must identify the mailing address and the residence (if different) of each inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also must identify any foreign application for which priority is claimed by specifying application number, country, and filing date (§1.63(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior executed oath in continuations/divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath is not required in a continuation or divisional application if (i) the prior nonprovisional contained a proper oath/declaration, (ii) the continuation/divisional filed by all or fewer inventors, (iii) the specification/drawings contain no new matter, and (iv) a copy of the executed prior oath/declaration showing signature (or indication of signature) is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fewer inventors are named, a statement requesting deletion of non-inventors must accompany the copy (§1.63(d)(1)-(2)). Special rules apply when prior application had §1.47 status (see §1.63(d)(3)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When new oath required for continuation/divisional/CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath/declaration must be filed in a continuation or divisional application naming an inventor not named in the prior application; a newly executed oath must be filed in any continuation-in-part application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.63(d)(5) and §1.63(e). CIPs always require a new executed oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement in lieu of oath (§1.64) — eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement may be executed when the inventor is deceased, under legal incapacity, has refused to execute the oath/declaration, or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applicants under §§1.43, 1.45, or 1.46 for applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 363 on/after Sept. 16, 2012 (editor note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement content and signer identification
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement must comply with §1.63(a) identifying the inventor with respect to whom it is executed; must identify the person executing the substitute statement, their relationship to the inventor, and unless supplied in an ADS, the residence and mailing address of the person signing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must also identify the circumstances permitting execution (deceased, legal incapacity, cannot be found, or refusal) and, unless in ADS, identify each inventor by legal name and last known mailing address for each inventor who is not deceased (§1.64(b)(1)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement signer must review application and acknowledge duty
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not execute a substitute statement unless that person has reviewed and understands the contents of the application, including the claims, and is aware of the duty to disclose to the Office all information known to the person to be material to patentability (§1.64(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements must contain an acknowledgment of criminal penalties for false statements (18 U.S.C.1001) (§1.64(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on nonsigning inventors and legal representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonsigning inventor or legal representative may subsequently join by submitting an oath/declaration under §1.63; such submission will not permit the nonsigning inventor or legal representative to revoke or grant a power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must make the oath/declaration (pre-AIA rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath/declaration (including supplemental oaths) must be made by all actual inventors except as provided in §§1.42, 1.43, 1.47, or §1.67. If the person making the oath is not the inventor, the oath must state the relationship and, upon information and belief, the facts required to be stated by the inventor; legal representative must state citizenship, residence, and mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.64 (pre-AIA) for detailed requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officers to administer oaths (domestic and foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath/affirmation may be made before any person within the U.S. authorized to administer oaths; in foreign countries, before U.S. diplomatic/consular officers or officers having an official seal and authorized to administer oaths, whose authority is proved by certificate or apostille. Oath must be attested by proper official seal; valid if it complies with laws where made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no seal is provided, official character must be evidenced by competent evidence, e.g., certificate from a court clerk (§1.66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign execution formalities (ribbon/seal and duplicate papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: When oath is taken before an officer foreign to the U.S., accompanying application papers (except drawings) must be attached with a ribbon passed through all sheets (except drawings) and the ends brought together under the seal, or each sheet must be impressed with the official seal. If not properly ribboned or sealed, the case will be accepted for examination but duplicate properly prepared papers must be filed before allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.66 (pre-AIA) for ribbon/seal requirements and consequences of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath or declaration to correct deficiencies (§1.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may submit a supplemental inventor’s oath or declaration meeting §1.63, §1.64, or §1.162 to correct deficiencies or inaccuracies in an earlier-filed oath/declaration; the supplemental oath must be executed by the person whose earlier oath is being withdrawn/replaced/corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies due to omitted mailing address (§1.63(c)) may be corrected with an application data sheet (§1.76). The Office will not require an additional oath if an oath complying with 35 U.S.C.115 and §1.63 or §1.162 was already executed. No new matter may be introduced even when correcting with supplemental oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a supplemental oath/declaration must be filed
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental oath/declaration meeting §1.63 must be filed when a claim is presented for matter originally shown or described but not substantially embraced in the original statement of invention or claims originally presented, or when an oath submitted after filing improperly refers to an amendment that includes new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In proper situations, the required oath may be made on information and belief by an applicant other than the inventor (§1.67(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration in lieu of oath (§1.68) — content and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: A written declaration may be used in lieu of an oath if the declarant is warned that willful false statements are punishable by fine or imprisonment (18 U.S.C.1001) and may jeopardize the validity of the application; declarant must state that own-knowledge statements are true and that statements on information and belief are believed to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an alternative to a sworn oath where statutes/rules permit (§1.68).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language oaths/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an individual making an oath/declaration cannot understand English, the oath/declaration must be in a language that the individual can understand and must state that the individual understands the content of the documents to which it relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-English oaths/declarations (unless in PTO form or per PCT Rule 4.17(iv)) must be accompanied by an English translation and a statement that the translation is accurate. For oaths under §1.63, the translation may be filed within two months after notification (§1.69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification — written description and enablement (§1.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include a written description of the invention and the manner and process of making and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must set forth the precise invention and distinguish it from other inventions and the prior art; describe a complete specific embodiment; explain mode of operation or principle when applicable; the best mode contemplated by the inventor must be set forth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification — improvements and scope of description
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an improvement, the specification must particularly point out the part(s) of the subject matter to which the improvement relates and the description should be confined to the specific improvement and parts that necessarily cooperate with it or are necessary to a complete understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits the required descriptive scope when claiming an improvement (§1.71(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright/mask work notice in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may be placed in a design or utility patent application adjacent to copyright/mask work material; the content of the notice must be limited to elements provided by law and the authorization language set forth in paragraph (e) must be included at the beginning of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example notices provided; inclusion permitted only if authorization language is included (see §1.71(d)-(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification formatting — separate sheet and exclusion of other parts
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must commence on a separate sheet. Each sheet including part of the specification may not include other parts of the application; the claim(s), abstract, and 'Sequence Listing' (if required) should not be included on a sheet including any other part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting requirement per §1.71(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement party names — disclosure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification may disclose or be amended to disclose the names of the parties to a joint research agreement; such amendment must be accompanied by the processing fee if not filed within certain time periods (e.g., within three months of filing, prior to first Office action, etc.). If filed after issue fee, the patent as issued may not include the names and correction may require certificate of correction (§1.71(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.71(g)(1)-(3) for the allowed time windows and fee consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements (§1.72)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention may not exceed 500 characters and must be as short and specific as possible. Unless supplied in an ADS, the title should appear as a heading on the first page of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters not capturable by Office automated systems may not be reflected in records (§1.72(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements (§1.72)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of the technical disclosure must commence on a separate sheet (preferably following the claims) under the heading 'Abstract' and must be as concise as disclosure permits, preferably not exceeding 150 words. Purpose: enable quick, cursory determination of the nature and gist of the technical disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract sheets may not include other parts of the application (§1.72(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the invention (§1.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary indicating the nature and substance of the invention, which may include a statement of the object of the invention, should precede the detailed description; it should be commensurate with the invention as claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any object recited should be that of the invention as claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to drawings (§1.74)
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are drawings, there shall be a brief description of the several views of the drawings; the detailed description shall refer to different views by figure numbers and to different parts by reference letters or numerals (preferably numerals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures clear cross-reference between description and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — general requirement to particularly and distinctly claim (§1.75(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must conclude with a claim particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the applicant regards as his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental statutory/formal requirement for claims placement and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple claims allowed and not unduly multiplied
rubrics_metrics.description: More than one claim may be presented provided they differ substantially from each other and are not unduly multiplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically applied to prevent excessive/duplicative claiming (§1.75(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims and multiple dependent claim rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims may refer back to and further limit another claim; multiple dependent claims must refer to other claims in the alternative only and may not serve as a basis for another multiple dependent claim. For fee calculation, a multiple dependent claim is considered to be the number of claims to which direct reference is made, and any claim depending from a multiple dependent claim is considered to be that number of claims to which direct reference is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original applications filed with or amended to include multiple dependent claims must include the fee set forth in §1.16(j). Dependent claims are construed to include all limitations of the claim incorporated by reference (§1.75(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must conform to specification and have antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim(s) must conform to the invention as set forth in the remainder of the specification and the terms/phrases used in the claims must find clear support or antecedent basis in the description so that their meaning may be ascertainable by reference to the description (§1.75(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.58(a) for related guidance on claim support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting order for improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the nature of the case admits (e.g., improvement), an independent claim should contain: (1) a preamble of general description of conventional/known elements; (2) a phrase such as 'wherein the improvement comprises,' and (3) those elements/steps/relationships constituting the new or improved portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested structure to clearly separate known elements from the improvement (§1.75(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering, order, and grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals; the least restrictive claim should be presented as claim number 1, and dependent claims should be grouped together with the claim(s) to which they refer to the extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational requirement to improve clarity and prosecution practice (§1.75(f)-(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims formatting — separate sheet and element separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page; any sheet including a claim may not contain other parts of the application. Where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step should be separated by a line indentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting rules intended to make claims clear and machine-processable (§1.75(h)-(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) — title, use, and when required (§1.76)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Application Data Sheet (ADS) must be titled 'Application Data Sheet' and may be submitted in provisional, nonprovisional, nonprovisional international design, or national stage applications; it must be submitted when required by §1.55 or §1.78 to claim priority or the benefit of a prior-filed application and, if provided, becomes part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADS must contain all section headings listed in paragraph (b) with appropriate data, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) (§1.76(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS — bibliographic data: inventor information
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS bibliographic data must include inventor information: legal name, residence, and mailing address of the inventor or each joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in ADS satisfies certain identification requirements and may obviate including it in the oath/declaration (§1.76(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS — bibliographic data: correspondence information
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS must include correspondence information, including the correspondence address which may be indicated by reference to a customer number to which correspondence is to be directed (§1.76(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence address reference ties to §1.33(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS — bibliographic data: application information
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS must include application information such as title of the invention, total number of drawing sheets, a suggested drawing figure for publication (nonprovisional), docket number, type of application, whether subject matter is under secrecy order, and, for plant applications, the Latin name and variety denomination. When referencing a previously filed application under §1.57(a), specify application number, filing date, and jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing previously filed application info in ADS constitutes replacing specification/drawings by reference when appropriate (§1.76(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS — bibliographic data: representative information
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS must include representative information such as the registration number of each practitioner having a power of attorney in the application (preferably by customer number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in ADS does not itself constitute a power of attorney (§1.76(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS — domestic benefit information
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS must include domestic benefit information: application number, filing date, status (including patent number if available), and relationship of each application for which a benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) (§1.76(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this in ADS constitutes the specific reference required by statute and §1.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS — foreign priority information
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS must include foreign priority information: application number, country (or intellectual property authority), and filing date of each foreign application for which priority is claimed. Providing this in ADS constitutes the claim for priority required by 35 U.S.C.119(b) and §1.55 (§1.76(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing priority data in ADS satisfies statutory priority claim formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS — applicant/assignee information
rubrics_metrics.description: ADS must include applicant information: name and address of the legal representative, assignee, person to whom inventor is under obligation to assign, or person showing sufficient proprietary interest who is the applicant under §1.43 or §1.46. Providing assignment information in ADS does not substitute for recording an assignment under part 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADS entry for applicant does not replace formal assignment-recording requirements (§1.76(b)(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting and updating an ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: An ADS that has been previously submitted may be corrected and updated (introductory paragraph begins §1.76(c)),
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text for full procedures is in paragraph (c) (chunk cut off); generally ADS corrections/updates are permitted subject to rules in §1.33 and §1.76.
